questions.question: How did the two glycine substitutions in RADA16 alter fibre morphology and hydrogel mechanics?

options.A: Middle-residue A8G formed bundled fibres and a more robust gel, whereas terminal A16G formed curved fibres and a softer, thixotropic gel
options.B: A8G formed curved fibres and a softer gel, whereas A16G formed bundled fibres and a stiffer gel
options.C: Both mutants formed identical straight fibres, but A16G had lower biocompatibility
options.D: A8G prevented gelation, whereas A16G formed a non-thixotropic hydrogel stiffer than RADA16

questions.rationale: The review contrasts the middle alanine-to-glycine mutant A8G with the terminal mutant A16G: flexibility does not produce the same supramolecular morphology or macroscopic stiffness in each position.
questions.evidence_quote: A8G, a mutant of RADA16 in which the alanine in the middle of the peptide sequence is replaced with glycine, forms bundled nanofibres and a more robust hydrogel than RADA16

questions.question: What feature of the A16G-N-cadherin construct accounted for its enhanced neuroblast migration relative to A16G alone?

options.A: N-cadherin was tagged to the self-assembling A16G peptide, displaying a migration-relevant adhesion cue on the fibrous scaffold
options.B: N-cadherin was replaced with VEGF, which induced neuroblast proliferation rather than migration
options.C: A16G was covalently crosslinked to RADA16, increasing gel stiffness without presenting a ligand
options.D: N-cadherin was mixed freely with the hydrogel, and the effect was independent of peptide tagging

questions.rationale: The A16G-Ncad conjugate couples a self-assembling peptide scaffold with N-cadherin, which is implicated in neuroblast migration along radial glial fibres.
questions.evidence_quote: Time-lapse imaging of ventricular-subventricular zone neuroblasts on culture dishes coated with A16G or a mixture of A16G and A16G-Ncad hydrogels showed that the migration rate of neuroblasts was significantly higher on the hydrogel containing A16G-Ncad than on A16G alone

questions.question: What molecular packing motif enables JigSAP's one-dimensional self-assembly?

options.A: An AXXXA hydrophobic motif undergoes an α-helix-to-β-strand transition and dovetail-like dimerization, promoting β-sheet nanofibre formation
options.B: A repeated RADA motif binds metal ions and forms cylindrical micelles through α-helical packing
options.C: A GXXXG motif remains permanently α-helical and forms fibres by covalent disulfide crosslinks
options.D: A histidine-rich motif coordinates Cu²⁺ at the membrane edge and drives phospholipid sheet assembly

questions.rationale: JigSAP contains an AXXXA motif; the conformational transition exposes a jigsaw-like hydrophobic surface that dimerizes by dovetail packing and supports β-sheet fibre assembly.
questions.evidence_quote: These motifs show α-helix-to-β-strand conformational transitions, generating a jigsaw-shaped hydrophobic surface that dimerizes with dovetail packing.

questions.question: How did JigSAP compare with 5V and RADA16 in protein incorporation and subsequent release?

options.A: EGFP-JigSAP incorporation was 93 mol%; after 168 h JigSAP released 39 mol%, versus 5 mol% for 5V and 8 mol% for RADA16
options.B: EGFP-JigSAP incorporation was 66 mol%; after 168 h it released 5 mol%, versus 39 mol% for 5V
options.C: Non-tagged EGFP incorporation was 93 mol%; all three gels released over 50 mol% by 24 h
options.D: JigSAP incorporation was 3 mol%; after 168 h it released 8 mol%, matching RADA16

questions.rationale: The peptide tag strongly improves incorporation, and JigSAP also permits greater long-term release than the other tagged peptide systems.
questions.evidence_quote: EGFP-JigSAP is incorporated at 93 mol%, whereas non-tagged EGFP is incorporated at only 3 mol%

questions.question: What biochemical distinction between JigSAP-IMI/ MII and their oxidized forms produced a stimulus-responsive gel-to-sol transition?

options.A: Methionine oxidation by ROS to methionine sulfoxide made the oxidized peptides remain dispersed, while unoxidized peptides formed gels
options.B: Reduction of disulfide bonds made the oxidized peptides gel, while unoxidized peptides remained soluble
options.C: Cu²⁺ binding crosslinked oxidized peptides into gels, while unoxidized peptides formed nanosheets
options.D: Photoisomerization of methionine changed peptide charge, causing only unoxidized peptides to disperse

questions.rationale: The Met residue is oxidized by reactive oxygen species to MetO; in the cited physiological conditions the oxidized variants are dispersed while their unoxidized counterparts form hydrogels.
questions.evidence_quote: remain dispersed in solution under a physiological condition (4 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, DMEM containing 1.0 wt% peptide concentration

questions.question: What role did Cu²⁺ play in stabilizing DPPC/Chol-MBP nanosheets upon dilution?

options.A: It crosslinked the PHGGG-containing Chol-MBP edge surfactants, preserving sheets at 0.2 wt% where uncrosslinked material formed sub-100-nm spherical aggregates
options.B: It dissolved the DPPC bilayer into micelles, preventing any morphological transition at 0.2 wt%
options.C: It bound DPPC headgroups and converted vesicles directly into nanosheets without Chol-MBP
options.D: It reduced the Chol-MBP peptide and caused the membrane edges to detach under dilution

questions.rationale: Histidine imidazoles in Chol-MBP bind Cu²⁺; Cu-mediated self-assembly at the sheet edge suppresses dissociation and preserves nanosheet morphology after dilution.
questions.evidence_quote: the nanosheet structure is maintained upon the same dilution process after the addition of 2.0 equivalents of Cu 2+ ions

questions.question: What was the key advantage of the DPPC/Chol-MBP/Cu nanosheet morphology in the mouse circulation comparison?

options.A: The nanosheets remained homogeneously dispersed in blood vessels, whereas fluorescent DPPC vesicles aggregated and clogged
options.B: The nanosheets rapidly fragmented into sub-100-nm spheres, whereas vesicles remained dispersed
options.C: The nanosheets were retained only in the liver, while vesicles circulated uniformly
options.D: The nanosheets induced endocytosis-like fission, whereas vesicles were unaffected by blood flow

questions.rationale: After tail-vein administration and intravital imaging, nanosheets were evenly distributed in vessels; vesicle aggregation and clogging contrasted with this behavior.
questions.evidence_quote: The FL DPPC vesicles were aggregated and clogged (Fig. 6f ), whereas FL DPPC/Chol-MBP/Cu nanosheets were homogeneously dispersed in the blood vessels

questions.question: How does the AzoMEx molecular machine induce endocytosis-like membrane fission?

options.A: Photoisomerization drives an opening-closing motion that changes the separation of two cationic NMe₃⁺ groups and expands the membrane
options.B: Cu²⁺-mediated peptide crosslinking contracts the bilayer and pulls in cargo
options.C: Oxidation of membrane phospholipids creates pores that passively admit virions
options.D: AzoMEx polymerizes into a rigid scaffold that mechanically tears the membrane

questions.rationale: AzoMEx is a photoresponsive amphiphile; its diazocine core changes conformation under light and mechanically expands the membrane to trigger outside-in fission.
questions.evidence_quote: which undergoes an opening-closing motion by photoisomerization to change the distance between two cationic NMe3 + moieties.

questions.question: What evidence indicates that AzoMEx-GUV delivery preserved M13 phage function and improved its persistence in blood?

options.A: Encapsulated phages remained infectious after reaching organs and showed higher blood stability than bare phages
options.B: Encapsulated phages lost infectivity but accumulated at higher concentration in the brain than spleen
options.C: Bare phages remained infectious, while encapsulated phages were rapidly cleared from blood
options.D: Phages were detected only in the blood vessels and no organ infectivity assay was performed

questions.rationale: The paper reports higher blood stability for encapsulated versus bare fluorescent phage and plaque-assay evidence of retained infectivity in multiple organs.
questions.evidence_quote: Importantly, even after distribution to the respective organs through the blood circulation, infectivity of M13 phages was retained

questions.question: Which factor most limited the review's proposed route for future biomedical application of dynamic bio-interface materials?

options.A: The materials science for reconstructing biomimetic interfaces with dynamic nature was described as still in its infancy
options.B: The supramolecular materials lacked any demonstrated regenerative or delivery function
options.C: All peptide scaffolds required toxic metal ions for self-assembly
options.D: The systems were only compatible with static interfaces and could not be tuned by stimuli

questions.rationale: The conclusion notes that this materials science remains at an early stage despite promising demonstrations in neuronal repair and cargo delivery.
questions.evidence_quote: The materials science to reconstruct biomimetic interfaces with a dynamic nature is still in its infancy and is expected to make significant progress in the future toward biomedical applications.
